heading: How a deal is put together.
lede: Single-asset and small-portfolio LLCs, syndicated deal by deal. Investors see the specific property, the specific budget and the specific terms before committing — no blind pool.

stack.what: Passive capital. Quarterly reporting, annual K-1, preferred return paid before any sponsor promote.
Sponsor. Sources, underwrites, signs on the debt, and carries co-investment alongside LP capital.
Bank or agency financing sized so the asset services it in a downside case, with an interest reserve funded at close for construction and lease-up.
Operating affiliate. Construction, renovation delivery and property management on market terms.

waterfall.caption: Distribution waterfall — Ohio Value-Add Portfolio I

rows.label: 01 — Preferred return
rows.detail: To limited partners, accrued if not paid currently

rows.label: 02 — Return of capital
rows.detail: 100% of invested capital returned at sale

rows.label: 03 — First split
rows.detail: Until a 15% limited partner IRR is achieved

note.title: Alternative structure under consideration
note.body: A three-class version — Class A for current income with capped upside, Class B for growth, Class C for investments above $500,000 — would widen the investor pool but complicates the operating agreement, the waterfall model and the reporting. For a first institutional raise the single-class structure above is simpler to document and to explain. Both are set out in the offering deck.
